note: Real briefs, not smoke tests: each is a request somebody would actually bring to 「虚拟临研」's analysis steps, chosen for the specific way an analysis goes wrong while looking finished — a weighted comparison whose effective sample size nobody looked at, a simulation whose null scenario was never run, a synthetic cohort quietly counted as patients. mustDo / mustNotDo are the rubric; the deterministic half (the four counts apart, an mcse on every simulated measure, a named interval kind, a not-estimable verdict with its rule) is the three vcr contracts in @evimed/domain plus this capability's preflight.

briefs.title: 三个方案并排：单臂 + 文献对照、2:1 随机、1:1 随机加一次期中分析
briefs.why: The ordinary full case (plan §10.3): the question a sponsor actually asks before a go/no-go. The failure that looks like success is a power table with no Monte-Carlo error and no null scenario — every number in it looks exact and none of them can be told from noise.
mustDo: Queue every design through vcr_simulate and report only what the engine returned.
Run a null-effect scenario for each design and report the type-I error from it.
Report every simulated measure with its Monte-Carlo standard error.

Compute the fixed design's sample size and the sequential boundaries analytically first, then cross-check them by simulation, and say so when the two differ by more than three Monte-Carlo standard errors.
State assurance separately from power, and say that it averages over the assumption's whole distribution rather than one point value.
State the four counts apart for every design, with generatedRecords for the simulated arms and realPatients null at T0.
Name the interval kind for every interval printed.
Say which design is dominated only if a saved comparison goal makes it decidable, and say whose goal it is.
mustNotDo: Type a power, a sample size or an event count that no job returned.
Present a simulated number without its Monte-Carlo standard error.
Call one design 'best' without a written comparison goal.
Count the simulated records of the external-control arm as real patients.
Fill a measure the engine could not compute with a 0.
briefs.gradedOn: Whether a statistician could take the operating-characteristics table and reproduce the ordering, and whether every number in the prose came from a job.

briefs.title: 「这个单臂试验能不能用外部对照？」（附数据字典，T2）
briefs.why: The feasibility question, and the one where the honest answer is most often 「不可估计」. The failure mode is an effect estimate produced anyway: entropy balancing converges on a degenerate solution, the effective sample size collapses, and a hazard ratio with a tight interval comes out of a comparison that is not one.
mustDo: Check ICH E10's four conditions before choosing a route, and say which of them hold.
Go through the FDA externally-controlled-trials draft's ten comparability dimensions one by one and record a finding for each.
Queue the weighting through vcr_simulate and read the diagnostics back: overlap, standardized differences after weighting, effective sample size.
Return conclusion not_estimable with the deterministic rule that fired and a gap list when any of the seven rules is triggered, and treat that as a finished result.
State the estimand the weighting answers (ATT by default) and say what changing it would mean.
Keep realPatients and effectiveSampleSize apart, and never let the effective sample size exceed the real patients it weights.
Name the interval kind, and use a bootstrap interval where weights were estimated.
mustNotDo: Produce an effect estimate when a not-estimable rule fired.
Report an effective sample size larger than the number of real patients weighted.
Use a synthetic or literature-derived cohort as if it were a real external control.
Describe the comparison as 「可比」 without the standardized differences that support it.
Drop a comparability dimension because the data says nothing about it — say the data says nothing.
briefs.gradedOn: Whether the run reached a defensible verdict — including 「不可估计」 with its gaps — rather than an estimate it could not support.

briefs.title: 「把我们上传的队列生成一份可以外发的合成数据」
briefs.why: The single-step data request. Two things go wrong quietly: the synthetic rows get counted as patients somewhere downstream, and the package ships with no leakage assessment, so nobody can tell whether a real person is recoverable from it.
mustDo: Queue the synthesis through vcr_simulate (synthesize_population) and report only what the engine returned.
Ship a quality report with fidelity, utility and disclosure-risk sections.
Set allowedUses to the uses a synthetic population may carry, and say in the report that a real external control is not one of them.
State generatedRecords and realPatients apart, and say plainly that generating more records does not create patients.
Give the screening waterfall with 「无法判断」 counted separately at every step.
Say which fields could not be synthesised faithfully and what that costs a downstream analysis.
mustNotDo: Report the synthetic row count as a sample size.
Let a 'design' or 'shared_preview' use be read as permission to use the cohort as an external control.
Fold 「无法判断」 into 「排除」 in the waterfall.
Quote a fidelity metric the engine did not return.
briefs.gradedOn: Whether a data-protection reviewer could read the quality report and decide whether the file may leave the building.

briefs.title: 「这个方案的 I 类错误到底是多少？」——问题落在零效应情景上
briefs.why: Live acceptance on production (2026-10-04): three design.analytic jobs asked for the required events or patients of a scenario with no effect (hazard ratio 1; equal control and treatment rates) and failed with no reason anyone could read. What the asker wanted was the design's type I error, which no closed-form sample size answers: it is the simulation's measure on the null scenario. The failure that looks like success is a type I error written as the nominal alpha, or as 0, because the analytic job returned nothing and the run filled in what it expected.

inputs.asked: 这个设计在没有效应时的 I 类错误是多少？

mustDo: Measure the type I error by queueing design_simulation on the null scenario (the same truth, with nTreat and nControl stated) and report the type_one_error measure the engine returned, with its Monte-Carlo standard error.

When a design_analytic job on a null effect comes back failed with design_effect_null, read the refusal's sentence, say in the report that a closed-form size does not exist without an effect, and continue with the simulation instead of asking the analytic job again in other words.
Compare the simulated type I error with the stated alpha in Monte-Carlo standard errors, and say so when it is outside them.
Read a failed job's own reason from vcr_simulate status and say what it was; a failed job always carries one.
Size the design for the effect it is meant to detect with design_analytic, as a separate question with its own non-null scenario.
mustNotDo: Ask design_analytic for the required size of a scenario whose hazard ratio is 1, whose effect is 0, or whose two rates are equal.
Write the nominal alpha, a zero or a remembered number as the type I error of a design.
Poll a failed job, or re-queue the same refused scenario unchanged.
Report an analytic sample size for the null scenario, or present the sample size of the alternative as the answer to a type I error question.
briefs.gradedOn: Whether a statistician could take the reported type I error, see which job produced it and with what Monte-Carlo error, and see that the run understood why the closed-form job had refused.
